text: A browser for coding agents on macOS, built on WebKit (Safari's engine). I run several coding agents at once, and Playwright's Chrome windows kept stealing my keyboard, while headless browsers got blocked by some sites and left me guessing what went wrong. agweb is one window that never takes focus: agents drive it from the shell with agweb , a playwright-cli-style command, and you watch them all live. Idle tabs are suspended: on my Mac five open pages sit at 0% CPU, where Chrome's GPU process kept five to seven cores busy. Needs macOS 26 or later. Download Agweb.dmg from Releases , drag Agweb to Applications and open it. Then Help ▸ Install Command Line Tool and Help ▸ Install Agent Skill (for Claude Code and Codex). Both are links into the app, so they update with it. To build from source instead (Xcode 26 or later): ./scripts/build.sh build/Agweb.app/Contents/Helpers/agweb install-cli agweb install-skill Use agweb -w task open en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WebKit # a workspace for this task; starts the app if needed agweb -w task snapshot # the page as a tree with [ref=eN] handles agweb -w task click ' role=button[name="Main menu"] ' The click's reply already says what it did, so the agent needs no second snapshot: ### Changes - navigation "Site" [ref=e2] - - button "Main menu" [ref=e3] + - button "Main menu" [checked] [expanded] [ref=e3] + - list [ref=e1167] + - listitem [ref=e1168] + - link "Main page" [ref=e1169] agweb help lists every command. Settings (⌘,) has text size, dashboard columns, a CPU and memory readout and the ad blocker switch. Same commands where possible, so agents already know them; a Playwright name it lacks suggests its own ( scroll-to → scroll-into-view ). On top: ./scripts/selftest.sh runs every command against a local page in a separate instance; swift test runs the unit tests. AGWEB_ROOT=/tmp/dir starts a second instance beside your own that keeps everything in that folder. Defuddle (MIT) is bundled for text .
